C1.claim: stime is 0.00% out of order across all 4 raw files; the data is strictly sorted by stime; a 10 s watermark is adequate.
C1.summary: The raw dataset is strictly chronologically ordered by flow completion time (ltime, 0.00% inversions across 2,540,047 rows), NOT stime. stime has 13.62% pairwise inversions (345,831 rows) and 19.20% running-max lateness (487,787 rows). A 10 s watermark drops 1.2666% of traffic (32,172 flows); a 60 s watermark is required (drops only 0.0014% = 36 flows). The prior report was caused by a column indexing bug in scripts/measure_lateness.py:35 which read ltime as stime and sintpkt as ltime.

C2.claim: The attack burst replayed through Spark was detected in ~3 s.
C2.summary: The 2,000 records replayed in run_spark_kafka_benchmark.py were drawn from File 1 (Session 0), which formed the training set of rf_detector.joblib (100% overlap). The ~3 s detection latency measured in-sample memorization rather than real-time anomaly detection. Re-evaluating on 10,000 unseen rows from Session 1 (File 3) containing 2,466 attacks across 136 bursts revealed steady-state flow processing latency of p50 = 5.86 s and p95 = 12.39 s (warm-up Batch 0 p50 = 2.86 s).

C3.claim: Window false-alarm rate on pure-normal windows is 0.04% at k=1, ~300x lower than the independent-flags prediction (13.87%), because false positives cluster on specific connections.
C3.summary: Connection clustering is empirically confirmed: the top-10 connection tuples account for 60.58% of all false-positive flows (> 50% threshold). In Session 0 (7,483 pure-normal 5-second tumbling windows), the false alarm rate is 0.0134% (1 flagged window) at k=1, and drops to 0.0000% (0 false alarms) at k=3. 100% of flagged pure-normal windows are clustered within 5 seconds of an attack window.

C4.claim: The elevated cross-session permutation AUC (S0->S1 mean 0.58) is caused by distribution shift between capture days, not leakage.
C4.summary: A clean 4-way label permutation decomposition (25 iterations each, 100 total Random Forest fits) confirmed that both intra-session tests are strictly at chance (Condition a Intra-S0 mean AUC = 0.5161, 95% CI [0.4790, 0.5532]; Condition c Intra-S1 mean AUC = 0.5196, 95% CI [0.4870, 0.5523]; both contain 0.50). Zero label leakage exists. In contrast, cross-session permutation in Condition b (S0->S1) yields an elevated mean AUC of 0.6194 (95% CI [0.5486, 0.6903]), confirming that elevation is driven entirely by covariate shift between capture days.
